findings.claim: The ONS Census, for example, covers the entire UK population at ten-year intervals.
findings.truth: ONS is responsible for the census in England and Wales; Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate census authorities. The England and Wales census takes place every ten years.
findings.evidence: ONS Census page, fetched 2026-09-03, lines 56 and 117-122

findings.claim: The UK Census, conducted every ten years, aims to record information about every household.
findings.truth: The ten-year census referred to by ONS is its England and Wales census, not a census administered by ONS for the whole UK.
findings.evidence: ONS Census page, fetched 2026-09-03, lines 56 and 117-122

findings.truth: Quota sampling is Additional Foundation content, so it must not be marked as Higher-only.

findings.claim: A sample frame is a complete list of every member of the population.
findings.truth: A sample frame is the list of population members available for sampling; the specification notes that not all of a population may be available for sampling.
The investigation approached 80 students, so 8 non-responders are out of 80.

findings.claim: The mark scheme proposes 8-10 and then 10 or more as category corrections.
findings.truth: Those categories overlap at 10. A non-overlapping exhaustive ending is 8-9 and 10 or more.
findings.evidence: recomputation of the stated category boundaries

findings.claim: The actual sampling method used within each stratum is then random sampling.
findings.truth: The specification says that stratification is used before sampling but does not prescribe the later sampling method. Either retain this as an explanation of stratified random sampling, or revise all related text to say that a sampling method is chosen within each stratum.

summary: Six verified surgical fixes were recorded. One statement about the method used after stratification needs an editorial decision and was not edited.
